stem: Drag the legs to make a right-angled triangle in which $\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$. Any size of triangle that works is correct: it is the ratio that has to match.
solution: $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$, so $\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ means the hypotenuse must be $\sqrt{2}$ times the adjacent side.
Take the adjacent side as 1 and the hypotenuse as $\sqrt{2}$. The Theorem of Pythagoras gives the other leg: $\text{opposite}^2 = (\sqrt{2})^2 - 1^2 = 1$, so the opposite side is also 1.

Drag the legs to equal lengths. Legs 1 and 1 work, and so do 3 and 3 or 5 and 5, because the ratio does not depend on the size of the triangle. For legs 5 and 5 the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{5^2+5^2} = 5\sqrt{2}$, so $\cos\theta = \dfrac{5}{5\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

Read the other two readouts on this triangle: $\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $\tan\theta = 1$. A right-angled triangle with equal legs has equal acute angles, so each is $45^\circ$. That is where $\cos 45^\circ = \sin 45^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $\tan 45^\circ = 1$ come from.
notes: Only the 45 degree values are reachable by a lattice drag: equal legs give cos = 1/sqrt(2) exactly (hypotenuse sqrt(2) x leg), whereas 30 and 60 degrees need legs in the ratio 1:sqrt(3) (see the gap for this objective). The target is the double nearest 1/sqrt(2), well inside any grading tolerance. used-sine is deliberately NOT mapped: a triangle with sin = 1/sqrt(2) has equal legs, so its cos is the target too and it is simply correct. off-target is not mapped (no single error dominates). used-tangent fires only if the tangent readout lands within the grader's tolerance of 0.7071 (for example legs 5 and 7 give 0.714); if the tolerance is tighter it will rarely fire, and the student gets a plain 'not quite'. Other errors of the objective (upside-down fraction, values from the other triangle, calculator decimals) cannot be expressed by this construction: an upside-down cos would be sqrt(2), above 1 and unbuildable. This template reverses the book's MCQ (the stem hands over the value and asks for the triangle), which is deliberate: it is the book's own derivation of the 45 degree values from the 1, 1, sqrt(2) triangle.
